purpose: Summative performance task for the full unit. Each child picks a rule (repeating, growing, or shrinking), builds an animal parade, translates it to a number parade with whole numbers up to 100, organizes it as a table of values, and justifies the rule. Used as primary summative evidence for C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, and C1.4.
student_learning_goal: I can build a number parade up to 100, name its rule, organize it as a table of values, and lead it.

parts.student_instructions: You are the Conductor today. Pick your rule and write it in the My Rule box. Circle the type. Then draw the part that will repeat (for repeating) or the first 2 terms (for growing/shrinking) in the My Core box.

MIDDLE: 'Pattern Type:' box (~2.5in × 1in, three circle options labelled REPEATING / GROWING / SHRINKING). RIGHT: 'My Core or First 2 Terms:' workspace box (~3in × 1.5in, blank). Below: a horizontal four-animal reference legend (Bea, Finn, Bibi, Moss). Beside the boxes, a small hundred-chart thumbnail (0-100) for number reference.

parts.answer_key: My Rule box: any valid rule label (AB / ABB / AAB / ABC for repeating; +1 to +10 for growing; -1 to -10 for shrinking). Type circle: matches the rule. Core box: shows the repeating core or the first 2 terms of the growing/shrinking pattern. The rule and core/terms must match — a child writing '+3' but drawing 1 then 2 Beas needs a conference.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Build animal parade and number parade
parts.student_instructions: Use your rule to fill all 8 cells of the animal parade. Then write the matching number for each term in the number parade strip below. Make sure your numbers stay between 0 and 100!
parts.visual_layout: An 8-cell horizontal parade strip labelled 'My Animal Parade' above. Each cell ~0.85in × 0.85in. Below it, a row of 8 boxes labelled 'My Number Parade' for the matching number values. Each cell numbered 1-8 below. Below: 'My starting number: ____'. To the side, the four-animal reference legend.

image_placeholders.description: An empty 8-cell horizontal parade strip in B&W line-art labelled 'My Animal Parade' above. All 8 cells blank with solid light-grey outlines. Below each cell, the number 1-8 printed in tiny grey text. Footprints beneath the strip. Full width.
A row of 8 empty boxes (~0.85in × 0.85in) labelled 'My Number Parade' above. Each box sized to hold a 1-3 digit number. Below each box, the cell number 1-8 printed in tiny grey text. Full width.

parts.answer_key: An 8-cell parade following the rule the child wrote in Part 1, with a matching 8-term number sequence where all values are between 0 and 100. Examples: Rule AB with Bea/Finn → animal parade Bea-Finn x 4 → numbers might be 5, 10, 5, 10, 5, 10, 5, 10. Rule +5 starting at 5 → 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. Rule -3 starting at 24 → 24, 21, 18, 15, 12, 9, 6, 3. Correct if the rule is preserved across both reps AND all numbers ≤ 100 AND ≥ 0.

parts.student_instructions: Fill in the Value column of the table with your 8 number-parade values. Then answer the questions at the bottom.
parts.visual_layout: A 2-column table of values centred on the page. 9 rows (1 header + 8 data). Headers TERM and VALUE. Term column pre-filled 1-8. Value column blank. Below the table: 'My rule works because ____' (writing line). Below that: 'Term 10 of my parade would be ____ (use the rule, not drawing!)'.

image_placeholders.description: A 2-column table of values, ~3.5in wide × 4in tall. 9 rows (1 header + 8 data). Headers TERM and VALUE in bold uppercase. Term column pre-filled 1-8. Value column empty. Thin black borders. K/G2-readable type.

A small hundred-chart thumbnail showing 0-100 in a 5x10 grid (each cell ~0.3in square). Numbers in clear K/G2-readable type. Light-grey grid lines. Approximately 1.8in × 3.5in total. Provided as a reference for children predicting term 10.
image_placeholders.placement: To the side of the table in Part 3.

parts.answer_key: Value column: copies the 8 numbers from Part 2 in matching term order. Justify sentence: any reasonable explanation referencing the rule (e.g., 'My rule is +5 and I added 5 each time' or 'My rule is AB so the parade alternates 5 and 10'). Term 10 prediction: depends on the rule. For +5 starting at 5, term 10 = 50. For AB pattern with values 5 and 10, term 10 = 10 (even terms = B = 10). For -3 starting at 24, term 10 = 24 - 9×3 = -3 — but that violates the ≥0 constraint, so the child should have picked a higher starting number; if they didn't, conference about constraint awareness.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and try a DIFFERENT pattern type. If you did growing, try shrinking now (or vice versa). Build the new parade and table.
teacher_notes: SUMMATIVE worksheet — the most important artifact in the unit. Score each completed worksheet against the 4-level rubric (see assessment_suite). Look for: (1) Did the rule, type, and core/terms match in Part 1? — C1.3 evidence. (2) Did the 8 animal cells follow the rule? — C1.1 evidence. (3) Did the number parade preserve the rule with numbers 0-100? — C1.4 evidence. (4) Did the table of values use correct headers AND correct values? — C1.2 evidence. (5) Did the justify sentence reference the rule, not just describe the parade? — C1.3 deepest evidence. (6) Did the term-10 prediction use the rule, not drawing? — C1.3 + C1.4 capstone.
